title: Sperling partial report (Sperling, 1960, Experiments 3 and 4)
summary: A card of 6 to 12 letters (or letters and numbers) is flashed for 50 ms. A cue then calls one row, and the observer types that row. The row's accuracy times the number of rows estimates how many letters were available when the cue came: about twice the 4 or so a whole report gives, falling to that span within a second as the cue is delayed. The paper's cue is a tone; this version uses a bar beside the row by default, because alhazen 2.16.0 cannot play an event-bound tone.
references: Sperling, G. (1960). The information available in brief visual presentations. Psychological Monographs: General and Applied, 74(11, Whole No. 498), 1-29. https://doi.org/10.1037/h0093759
Averbach, E., & Coriell, A. S. (1961). Short-term memory in vision. Bell System Technical Journal, 40(1), 19-31.

deviations.original: A tone after the exposure: high 2500, middle 650, low 250 cps, about 0.5 s, from an audio oscillator switched by the light's off-go microswitch (p. 6-7)
deviations.here: Default cue_mode: visual, a bar beside the cued row for 0.5 s, starting at the same frame the tone would (an Averbach and Coriell style marker). cue_mode: tone binds the paper's three tones to the CUE_HIGH, CUE_MID and CUE_LOW events, but refuses to load on alhazen 2.16.0
deviations.reason: alhazen 2.16.0 cannot play a tone bound to a task event. A visual cue near the array is not equivalent to an auditory one: it can mask or attract attention to the location, so results can differ from the paper's

deviations.original: Gerbrands two-field mirror tachistoscope, 4-watt daylight fluorescent lamps, a 50 ms flash whose phosphor afterglow decays in two parts (about 40% of the energy in under 1 ms, the yellow rest with a time constant of about 15 ms; Fig. 1, p. 3)
deviations.here: A computer display: the card is shown for whole frames at the measured refresh rate (3 frames = 50.0 ms at 60 Hz; 7 = 48.6 ms at 144 Hz), recorded per trial with the flip-stamped exposure. An LCD holds each frame and its pixels settle in a few ms; an OLED switches in well under 1 ms. Neither reproduces the lamp's 15 ms afterglow
deviations.reason: No tachistoscope. The exposure's energy profile and offset differ from Fig. 1; docs/methods.md, Apparatus, sets out what that changes

deviations.original: Written on a response grid on the table below the tachistoscope, by room light; S slid the paper under a cover after each report (p. 4)
deviations.here: Typed into a row of boxes on the screen; BACKSPACE corrects, ENTER commits once every box is filled
deviations.reason: Keyboard entry keeps the response in the data file; scoring by position (p. 4) is unchanged

deviations.original: The 21 consonants (in a few card sets also without Y, p. 3); 20 letters plus the ten digits on letters-and-numbers cards (17.9 bits per row, p. 4)
deviations.here: 17 consonants, BDFGJKLMNQSTVWXYZ: C, H, P and R are left out, on every material
deviations.reason: alhazen 2.16.0 reads its experimenter keys (p pause, c calibrate, r reward, h hold stage) from the same keyboard before the subject's keys, so a subject cannot type those letters. Fewer alternatives make a guess slightly likelier (1/17 vs 1/21 per position)

deviations.original: High, middle and low tones exactly equally often per material, balanced over several sessions, usually two (p. 7)
deviations.here: Balanced within every delay block: 6 test trials per block, 2 per row for three rows (3 per row for two), in random order
deviations.reason: A session is analysed on its own here, so each block carries its own balance

deviations.original: An observer who wrote the wrong row was asked to write what he could remember of the correct row; only the indicated row was scored (p. 7)
deviations.here: Only the cued row is scored; reports that match another row better are counted (other_row_max_correct) but there is no second report
deviations.reason: Software cannot tell a misheard cue from a poor report while the trial runs

deviations.original: Twelve sessions per observer, three a week; 30 training trials per two-row material in each of the first two sessions; up to 150 more for one observer; strategy instructions changed half-way (p. 4, p. 7, p. 11)
deviations.here: One session per parameter set; training is the sample trials (2 per block) only
deviations.reason: The multi-session training schedule is the experimenter's to run, by repeating sessions

deviations.original: The dark field and the dim fixation field were always present (p. 3)
deviations.here: The task draws the dark field and cross on every frame of a trial; for the frames between one trial's end and the next trial's start, and on instruction and pause screens, the window shows alhazen's mid-grey background
deviations.reason: alhazen 2.16.0 has no setting for the window's background colour

deviations.original: Over 500 hand-lettered 5x8 in cards; no observer reported the same part of a card more than two or three times (p. 3)
deviations.here: A new random card is generated for every trial (independent uniform draws, as the paper's information values assume)
deviations.reason: Generated arrays are reproducible from the session seed and never repeat by design

deviations.original: Binocular, through the tachistoscope, at about 24 in (cards at 22 in, p. 3)
deviations.here: Binocular, at the rig file's viewing distance; every size is in degrees of visual angle
deviations.reason: Sizes are kept in visual angle rather than inches

deviations.original: Part 2's wording (p. 11): "You will hear a tone during the flash or while it is fading which will indicate which letters you are to attempt to read. Do not read the card until you hear the tone"
deviations.here: The same wording with the bar in place of the tone (instructions.md); instructions-tone.md keeps the tone; both add the key rules
deviations.reason: The cue modality changed, and the keyboard needs explaining

tasks.title: Partial report with a delayed row cue
tasks.summary: SPACE starts; 0.5 s later the card is shown for 50 ms; a cue at a set delay from its offset calls a row; the observer types that row and presses ENTER.
tasks.description: One task runs every parameter set: Experiment 4's decay (configs/task.yaml, 12 letters and numbers; configs/task-9.yaml, 9 letters), Experiment 3 at zero delay on all four materials (configs/task-exp3.yaml), and Experiment 1's whole report (configs/task-whole.yaml).

parameters.name: report
parameters.label: Report
parameters.meaning: partial: type the cued row (Exp. 3 and 4). whole: type every symbol (Exp. 1, the immediate-memory baseline).

parameters.name: materials
parameters.label: Materials
parameters.meaning: Cards run in this session, in order: 3/3, 4/4, 3/3/3, 4/4/4-LN (two letters and two numbers per row).

parameters.name: cue_mode
parameters.label: Cue
parameters.meaning: visual: a bar beside the cued row (the default; a deviation). tone: the paper's high, middle and low tones; refuses to load until alhazen has Tone.

parameters.name: cue_delays_s
parameters.label: Cue delays
parameters.meaning: Cue onset from the array's offset, one block per delay; -0.10 is 0.05 s before the array's onset.

parameters.name: cue_duration
parameters.label: Cue duration
parameters.meaning: The tone's length; the bar lasts as long (ASSUMED for the bar).

parameters.name: first_series
parameters.label: First series
parameters.meaning: Direction of the first series of delay blocks; series alternate.

parameters.name: n_series
parameters.label: Series
parameters.meaning: Series of delay blocks per material.

parameters.name: samples_per_block
parameters.label: Samples per block
parameters.meaning: Sample (practice) trials before each delay block; not analysed.

parameters.name: paradigm.n_per_condition
parameters.label: Test trials per block
parameters.meaning: Test trials in each delay block, rows balanced within it. ASSUMED, not in the paper (it says five or more).

parameters.name: exposure
parameters.label: Exposure
parameters.meaning: How long the card is shown, in whole frames at the measured refresh rate.

parameters.name: start_delay
parameters.label: Start delay
parameters.meaning: From the observer's SPACE press to the card.

parameters.name: report_timeout
parameters.label: Report deadline
parameters.meaning: A trial with no committed report by then is served again. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: tone_high_hz
parameters.label: High tone
parameters.meaning: Tone for the top row (tone mode).

parameters.name: tone_mid_hz
parameters.label: Middle tone
parameters.meaning: Tone for the middle row of three-row cards (tone mode).

parameters.name: tone_low_hz
parameters.label: Low tone
parameters.meaning: Tone for the bottom row (tone mode).

parameters.name: consonants
parameters.label: Consonants
parameters.meaning: Letters drawn for the cards; C, H, P and R are refused (alhazen's experimenter keys).

parameters.name: letter_height_dva
parameters.label: Letter height
parameters.meaning: Capital height: 0.45 in at 22 in.

parameters.name: letter_pitch_dva
parameters.label: Letter spacing
parameters.meaning: Centre-to-centre. ASSUMED, not in the paper (estimated from Fig. 2).

parameters.name: row_pitch_three_rows_dva
parameters.label: Row spacing, three rows
parameters.meaning: Centre-to-centre. ASSUMED, not in the paper (estimated from Fig. 2).

parameters.name: card_width_dva
parameters.label: Card width
parameters.meaning: 8 in at 22 in; landscape is ASSUMED.

parameters.name: fixation_color
parameters.label: Fixation cross colour
parameters.meaning: Signed RGB; 'dimly illuminated' (paper p. 3), the value ASSUMED.

outcomes.name: REPORTED
outcomes.meaning: A full report was committed with ENTER; it is scored per position afterwards (n_correct, letters_available).

outcomes.name: NO_RESPONSE
outcomes.meaning: No committed report before the deadline; served again at the end of its block.

outcomes.name: NO_START
outcomes.meaning: SPACE was not pressed before the start deadline; served again at the end of its block.

events.name: FIX_ON
events.meaning: The dark field and dim cross; the trial waits for SPACE.

events.name: ARRAY_ON
events.meaning: The card's first frame; payload: material and rows.

events.name: ARRAY_OFF
events.meaning: The first frame of the dark post-exposure field; cue delays are measured from it.

events.name: CUE_HIGH
events.meaning: The cue for the top row starts (the high tone in tone mode); payload: row and delay.

events.name: CUE_MID
events.meaning: The cue for the middle row of a three-row card (the 650 Hz tone).

events.name: CUE_LOW
events.meaning: The cue for the bottom row (the low tone).

events.name: REPORT_ON
events.meaning: Keys count from this frame; payload: what to report.

events.name: RESPONSE_BOXES_ON
events.meaning: The response boxes appear (when the cue ends).

events.name: RESPONSE
events.meaning: The report committed with ENTER; payload: the response.
